records.rule: Two 5×5 balls in a black maze; each press moves each ball 1 cell (right ball's LEFT/RIGHT mirrored, vertical normal). Adjacent balls visually merge. Goal (hypothesis, best fit): each ball must reach the opposite color's half — the swap happened on the final LEFT and won.

Goal = make the two 4×4 balls collide (head-on). Controls: left ball normal, right ball horizontally mirrored; walls block, red checkered cells are lethal (stepping on one resets both balls to start). Won by driving both down their sides through the spike-band gaps into the open bottom room, then pressing RIGHT when adjacent (A left of B) → head-on collision → LEVEL COMPLETED.

Goal = collide the two balls (left ball normal, right ball mirrored). Dark-blue tokens blocked corridors; MOUSE a token → it turns yellow and moves with normal arrows while balls freeze gray; MOUSE a ball → resume control. Parked all 3 tokens in dead-end cells, then drove the balls head-on (25 presses). Won on a RIGHT press when adjacent.

Goal = collide the two balls (left ball normal, right ball horizontally mirrored). Red-checker cells are LETHAL: stepping on one resets the entire level (balls AND the parked token), so hazards must be routed around, never treated as walls. MOUSE a token → it turns yellow and moves with normal arrows while balls freeze gray; MOUSE a ball → resume. Won by parking the token at (3,6), then DOWN,RIGHT,RIGHT,LEFT,UP,UP,RIGHT,RIGHT,RIGHT → head-on collision.

Goal = collide the two balls (left ball horizontally mirrored, right ball normal). Colored 4×4 blocks are BUTTONS: while a ball stands on a button cell, ALL blocks/bars of that color vanish; leaving restores them. Gates (3-cell bars) are passable only while their color's button is held. Won by: right ball holds green button → left ball passes green gate into top room → left ball holds purple button → right ball passes purple gate → head-on LEFT collision.

limitations: Tool-call source and tool result first appearing in a request snapshot are historical output already executed before that request, not actions caused by the request itself.
snapshot_crosscheck.delivery_counts_interpretation: 81 actual requests contain the memory header; the helper reports80 successful responses with memory. An attempted request is not silently counted as a successful delivery, and an unreturned request is not assumed to have zero cost.

overall_limit: The paired benchmark outcome is observed. Memory delivery counters and recorded rules do not establish correct reuse or a causal contribution to the score difference.

candidate_components: Post-completion instruction to state a Rule for level summary in the ordinary response, without a separate new model request.
Pin observed facts, action/reasoning tails and captured rules into system context when normal history is evicted.
component_attribution.finding: Both mechanisms occurred in the real trajectory. Improvements before the first pin are still temporally compatible with the reflection instruction once an earlier level has completed. They must not be dismissed merely because the system block had not yet appeared. Conversely, L1 discovery precedes both successful-experience mechanisms in that game.
component_attribution.causal_limit: This natural-start paired experiment tests the combined candidate. It does not isolate reflection from pinning, retained functions, ordinary history or model trajectory variation.

accurate_action_label.current_semantics: Actions recorded for that level since entry or the last explicit RESET represented in runtime history; may include probes, failed plans, and unflagged internal soft resets.
accurate_action_label.unchanged_facts: The true level-completion facts and model rule hypotheses remain distinct. The accounting label issue does not change benchmark actions, completed levels or score.
accurate_action_label.future_label_only_suggestion: If a later version is intentionally created, label the text as recorded level action history rather than latest successful attempt. No untested change is applied to this frozen helper, and no v2 efficacy is credited here.

review_conclusion: Both selected games show real post-completion reflection, actual memory delivery after history shrink, and subsequent executable transfer to current-level planning/actions. cd82 provides especially clear region-model reuse with checks and successive clears. m0r0 provides collision/token/gate transfer but also a concrete hazard-model regression and contaminated action tails after unflagged soft resets. These observations support that the combined candidate exercises real mechanisms; they do not isolate how much of the measured score gain comes from reflection or pinning. L1 discovery gains must remain outside memory attribution. This review does not add a gate or stop the already launched full comparison.
snapshot_crosscheck_method: Read only the two completed candidate request logs, matched actual system memory blocks to successful helper hashes, located exact captured rules using the frozen helper parser, and matched selected previously reviewed transcript tool code to request snapshots by code hash. No model/tool code replay, test, GPU or helper modification.
